page.layout: One printed page of text in a single column, with no marginal notes. Below the text: the closing line "FINIS ARCHELOGIÆ." and, at lower right, the catchword. The strip of text at the right edge belongs to the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

p.i: tibi gratias, ô Deus, ô principium principiorum, pro bonis illis donis, quæ in nos ubertim confers nil tale merentes. Magnum est, ô magne Deus, quòd aperuisti nobis Scholam naturæ, in quâ das nobis librum, quo te-ipsum manifestas, & accendis lumen, quo evolvimus istum librum discussis tenebris & nebulis mentis. Majus est, ô magne Pater, quòd aperuisti nobis Scholam Gratiæ, in quâ das nobis librum Scripturæ, in quo tuam voluntatem de nobis & à nobis discimus, & accendis lumen Gratiæ, quo freti legere possumus librum illum. Maximum denique est, ô maxime Pater, quòd nos tandem aliquando deduces in Scholam Gloriæ, ubi scientia sine disciplinâ, finis sine fine, collatio sine decessione, receptio sine accessione, quies sine motu, triumphus sine bello. Gratias igitur tibi agimus immortales, ô gratiose, ô gloriose, ô immortalis Deus, pro tantis hisce beneficiis. Rogamus te, Clementissime Pater, præbe Ecclesiis & Scholis halcyonia, adversus Satanam & administros ejus, & nobis in iis. Benedic vitæ, valetudini, studiis, & laboribus nostris. Duc nos viâ rectâ ad metam, quæ nobis in cælo reservatur ad divinæ tuæ gratiæ gloriam, per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, qui tecum & cum Spiritu sancto regnat & vivit, Deus benedictus in omne ævum, Amen Amen! Etiam Domine Jesu!

page.notes: The "Maximum denique" word shows a superscript mark after "deniq", read here as "denique" with the e-abbreviation uncertain. The catchword "JOH-" is set at the lower right below the last line, as printed. Greek and other scripts: none on this page. The right-edge strip is show-through or the neighbouring page and was not transcribed.
